title: Fourth Word Explaining The Comparison And Its Rational Measure

questions.question: In the comparison, who does the ruler stand for?
questions.answer: The ruler stands for Allah, our Sustainer and Creator.

questions.question: What do the two servants represent?
questions.answer: One stands for careful believers who pray sincerely, and the other stands for careless people who leave the prayers.

questions.question: What do the twenty-four gold coins mean in the comparison?
questions.answer: They mean the twenty-four hours of one day of life.

questions.question: What does the royal land represent?
questions.answer: It represents Paradise.

questions.question: What does the station represent?
questions.answer: It represents the grave.

questions.question: What does the journey represent?
questions.answer: It represents a person’s travel through life to the grave, then to resurrection and the hereafter.

questions.question: According to the passage, why do people travel that journey at different speeds?
questions.answer: Because their actions are different, and their level of fear of Allah is different.

questions.question: What does the ticket represent?
questions.answer: It represents the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: About how much time each day is needed for the five daily prayers and wudu?
questions.answer: About one hour.

questions.question: Why is it a serious loss to spend almost all day only on worldly life?
questions.answer: Because this world passes quickly, while the hereafter is much longer and more important.

questions.question: What example is used to show that leaving prayer is unreasonable?
questions.answer: The passage compares it to risking a lot on a weak chance of gain but refusing a small share for a much surer and greater reward.

questions.question: What good things does prayer bring to the inside of a person?
questions.answer: It gives comfort to the spirit, the heart, and the mind.

questions.question: How does the passage describe prayer for the body?
questions.answer: It says prayer is not hard for the body.

questions.question: With the right intention, what can happen to a praying person’s other daily actions?
questions.answer: They can also become acts of worship.

questions.question: How can a person make his temporary life lasting in one way?
questions.answer: By praying and having the right intention, so the deeds of this short life bring reward for the hereafter.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It speaks to people who do not pray and also to the speaker’s own self that resists prayer.

questions.question: In the comparison, what does the faithful servant show us?
questions.answer: He shows the example of a believer who performs the prayers eagerly and seriously.

questions.question: In the comparison, what does the neglectful servant show us?
questions.answer: He shows the example of a person who is careless and does not perform the prayers.

questions.question: Why is one day pictured as twenty-four coins?
questions.answer: To show that each hour is like a valuable part of our life that should be used wisely.

questions.question: What do Paradise and the grave teach us in this comparison?
questions.answer: They teach that life is moving toward the next world, so our choices now matter.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the length of the journey after death?
questions.answer: It teaches that it is very long and serious, and people pass through it according to their deeds.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention very fast travel over huge distances?
questions.answer: To show that righteous people can pass that journey with great ease and speed by Allah’s permission.

questions.question: Why is prayer compared to a ticket?
questions.answer: Because it is the means that prepares a person for the journey ahead.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the amount of time prayer takes?
questions.answer: It says the five prayers with ablution take only a small part of the day.

questions.question: Why is skipping prayer called unfair to oneself?
questions.answer: Because a person harms his own future by refusing something small that brings a huge reward.

questions.question: What does the passage say is easier to accept than neglecting prayer: giving away half of one’s wealth in a risky gamble or giving a small part for a certain treasure?
questions.answer: Giving a small part for a near-certain eternal reward is much wiser than risking a lot for a tiny chance.

questions.question: Besides reward in the hereafter, what benefit does prayer give in this life?
questions.answer: It brings peace and comfort to a person’s inner life.

questions.question: How can regular prayer change ordinary daily activities?
questions.answer: It can turn them into worship if the person has a good intention.

questions.question: Match each part of the comparison to its meaning: ruler, twenty-four coins, station, ticket.
questions.answer: Ruler means Allah; twenty-four coins mean the hours of one day; station means the grave; ticket means the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: Which servant is the better example to follow, and why?
questions.answer: The praying servant is better because he is careful about what really matters for the hereafter.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about life in this world compared with the life to come?
questions.answer: Life in this world is short and passing, but the life to come is long and lasting.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect daily time with wealth?
questions.answer: To help us understand that time is precious and should not be wasted.

questions.question: If one hour is used for prayer, what does that show about Allah’s commands?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah asks for something manageable and full of benefit.

questions.question: What mistake does the neglectful person make with his day?
questions.answer: He uses almost all of it for temporary worldly things and leaves out what benefits him forever.

questions.question: What idea does the example of a lottery help explain?
questions.answer: It explains that refusing prayer is not reasonable, because people chase weak chances in worldly matters but ignore a far greater reward.

questions.question: According to the passage, how sure is the reward of the eternal treasure compared with the lottery example?
questions.answer: The eternal reward is shown as being far more certain and trustworthy.

questions.question: Name three inner parts of a person that benefit from prayer.
questions.answer: The spirit, the heart, and the mind.

questions.question: Does the passage present prayer as crushing and exhausting for the body, or as manageable?
questions.answer: It presents prayer as manageable.

questions.question: What must a person have so that other daily actions can count as worship too?
questions.answer: The person must have the right intention.

questions.question: How does right intention affect the value of everyday actions?
questions.answer: It gives them reward for the hereafter.

questions.question: What does it mean that a person can send the capital of life to the hereafter?
questions.answer: It means he can use his time and deeds now to gain lasting reward later.

questions.question: What is one reason this passage encourages hope instead of laziness?
questions.answer: Because it shows that a small effort in prayer brings huge benefit.

questions.question: Who is compared to the king or ruler in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah, who created and cares for us.

questions.question: What kind of people are shown by the servant who does his duty well?
questions.answer: People who perform the daily prayers with eagerness and care.

questions.question: What kind of people are shown by the servant who is careless?
questions.answer: People who neglect the daily prayers.

questions.question: What does each day’s twenty-four-part gift remind us to do?
questions.answer: It reminds us to use our time wisely for both this life and the hereafter.

questions.question: Why is the grave called a station in the comparison?
questions.answer: Because it is a stopping place on the way to the next stage, not the final end.

questions.question: What comes after the grave in the journey described here?
questions.answer: Resurrection and the life of the hereafter.

questions.question: What affects how people move through that journey?
questions.answer: Their deeds and their fear of Allah.

questions.question: What is the small daily action that prepares a person for the big journey?
questions.answer: Performing the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: How much of the day does the passage ask for prayer and ablution?
questions.answer: About one hour.

questions.question: Why does the passage say a person harms himself by leaving prayer?
questions.answer: Because he gives nearly all his day to short-term things and neglects what helps him forever.

questions.question: What comparison is made with money and chance?
questions.answer: The passage compares neglecting prayer to acting foolishly with money by favoring a poor chance over a much surer and better gain.

questions.question: How does prayer help a person emotionally and mentally?
questions.answer: It gives peace and relief inside.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the physical difficulty of prayer?
questions.answer: It says prayer is not a heavy burden on the body.

questions.question: If a Muslim prays and keeps a good intention, what can happen to schoolwork, chores, and other lawful actions?
questions.answer: They can become worship too and bring reward for the hereafter.

questions.question: In this explanation, what is the most important meaning of the ticket?
questions.answer: It means the daily prayers that prepare a person for the next life.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the value of one hour used well?
questions.answer: One hour used for prayer can help a person gain great benefit for the hereafter.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the other twenty-three hours?
questions.answer: They should not make a person forget Allah and the life to come.

questions.question: Why is worldly life called fleeting?
questions.answer: Because it does not last long and passes away quickly.

questions.question: Why is the hereafter called long life in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it continues beyond this short world.

questions.question: What is unreasonable about the person described in the passage?
questions.answer: He cares more about a small, temporary life than about everlasting success.

questions.question: How does the example of gambling help make the point stronger?
questions.answer: It shows that people may spend a lot for a tiny chance, yet some still refuse a small effort for a much surer reward.

questions.question: What percentage of certainty is given for the eternal treasure in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as ninety-nine out of a hundred.

questions.question: What does prayer do for the soul and thoughts of a believer?
questions.answer: It brings comfort and rest to them.

questions.question: Is prayer shown as harmful to the body or suitable for it?
questions.answer: It is shown as suitable for it and not too hard.

questions.question: What is needed for normal actions to count as worship?
questions.answer: A correct and sincere intention.

questions.question: What does it mean to turn life’s capital toward the hereafter?
questions.answer: It means using one’s time, energy, and deeds for lasting reward.

questions.question: What overall choice does the passage urge the reader to make each day?
questions.answer: To give time to prayer and live with the hereafter in mind.

questions.question: What does this passage mainly try to persuade the reader to do?
questions.answer: It tries to persuade the reader to perform the five daily prayers.

questions.question: Why does the passage talk to the speaker’s own nafs as well as other people?
questions.answer: To show that the struggle against laziness in prayer is personal and real.

questions.question: In the comparison, what does Paradise show about the goal of life?
questions.answer: It shows that the true goal is success in the next world.

questions.question: What does the grave being called a station teach about death?
questions.answer: It teaches that death is a stage on the way, not the end of everything.

questions.question: According to the passage, do all people experience the next journey in the same way?
questions.answer: No. Their experience differs based on their deeds and their fear of Allah.

questions.question: Why are examples of very fast travel mentioned?
questions.answer: To show how greatly Allah can ease the journey for the righteous.

questions.question: What simple duty is given as the “ticket” for that journey?
questions.answer: The prescribed daily prayers.

questions.question: How does the passage answer someone who says prayer takes too much time?
questions.answer: It says the prayers and ablution together need only about one hour a day.

questions.question: What is the person really choosing if he spends all day for dunya and no time for prayer?
questions.answer: He is choosing short-term things over lasting benefit.

questions.question: Why is that choice described as a loss?
questions.answer: Because the person gives up something eternal for something temporary.

questions.question: What thinking mistake is shown by the lottery example?
questions.answer: It shows the foolishness of trusting a weak worldly chance while ignoring a much surer eternal reward.

questions.question: What are the three inner human parts named as receiving comfort from prayer?
questions.answer: The spirit, the heart, and the mind.

questions.question: What does the passage say about prayer and physical hardship?
questions.answer: It says prayer is not difficult for the body.

questions.question: How can one hour of worship affect the rest of the day?
questions.answer: With a good intention, it can help the rest of a person’s lawful actions gain worship value too.

questions.question: What is one sentence a student could say as the lesson of this passage?
questions.answer: Prayer is a small daily effort that brings peace now and great reward in the hereafter.
